findings.claim: Incorrectly collapsed: SHERPA_ONNX_LINK_LIBSTDCPP_STATICALLY=OFF proves Sherpa Android used dynamic libc++ or no static C++ runtime.
findings.reason: The observed Sherpa commands set BUILD_SHARED_LIBS=ON on Android with NDK r30. The fixed CMake guard applies the static GNU option block only under NOT BUILD_SHARED_LIBS AND CMAKE_SYSTEM_NAME STREQUAL Linux, where true adds -static-libstdc++ -static-libgcc. That branch is separate from Android NDK STL selection and from libc++/libc++abi/unwind retention.

findings.claim: Incorrectly collapsed: ORT r27d and Sherpa r30 both used the legacy toolchain branch because NDK toolchains default to legacy true.
findings.reason: Both supplied NDK toolchain files default to the legacy file only when ANDROID_USE_LEGACY_TOOLCHAIN_FILE is undefined. The ORT commands explicitly pass false, so the r27d legacy include-and-return branch is bypassed. The observed Sherpa commands do not pass that variable, so on the supplied command state the r30 default legacy branch applies; other cache state was not supplied.
findings.source: ORT arm64/armeabi-v7a/x86/x86_64 logs line 455; sherpa android-libs.log lines 778,1577,2338,3133; r27d and r30 android.toolchain.cmake lines 47-56

findings.claim: Incorrectly collapsed: all four Sherpa ABIs explicitly set SHERPA_ONNX_LINK_LIBSTDCPP_STATICALLY=OFF.
findings.reason: The arm64, armeabi-v7a, and x86_64 commands include that flag; the x86 command shown does not. This does not change the shared-Android guard analysis, but it does not support a claim of four explicit OFF settings.

findings.claim: Incorrectly collapsed: legacy NDK default c++_static or CMAKE_CXX_FLAGS -stdlib=libc++ proves final retained libc++, libc++abi, or unwind code.
findings.reason: The legacy files set ANDROID_STL c++_static only when ANDROID_STL is unset, and ORT bypasses legacy via false. The ORT flags show a C++ standard-library compile intent, not final link/retention. The supplied ELF evidence says DYNSYM/no SYMTAB, no libc++_shared DT_NEEDED, and std::__ndk1 exports do not establish retained implementation, exact version, static absence, or complete composition.
findings.source: r27d/r30 android-legacy.toolchain.cmake lines 241-242,357-372/366-381; ORT logs line 1139/1150/1146; elfEvidence

findings.claim: Incorrectly collapsed: reference-only local NDKs or release-tag source files prove the packaged runtime kit identity and full notice set.
findings.reason: The context explicitly marks 27.0.12077973 and 30.0.16138531-beta3 as reference-only local NDKs. Version bindings associate release tags with version snippets, but do not alone prove packaged kit identity, final composition, or applicable full notices.

findings.claim: The excerpts are sufficient to close notice applicability.
findings.reason: They establish selected build configuration and branch guards only. No supplied evidence maps all final SOs/AAR/Maven artifacts to runtime components, source packages, licenses, notice texts, or exclusions, so full-notice conclusions remain out of scope.

supportedClaims.claim: ORT was built against the toolchain path for NDK 27.3.13750724, bound in the supplied release bindings to r27d, with Clang 18.0.4, onnxruntime_BUILD_SHARED_LIB=ON, ANDROID_PLATFORM/MIN_SDK=27, ANDROID_USE_LEGACY_TOOLCHAIN_FILE=false, and CMAKE_CXX_FLAGS containing -stdlib=libc++.
supportedClaims.source: ORT arm64/armeabi-v7a/x86/x86_64 logs lines 455,493-494,1139/1150/1146; officialVersionBindings r27d

supportedClaims.claim: Sherpa was built in the supplied job against the toolchain path for NDK 30.0.16248370, bound in the supplied release bindings to r30, with Clang 21.0.0, BUILD_SHARED_LIBS=ON, JNI/C API enabled, and ANDROID_PLATFORM=android-21.

In both supplied NDK toolchain files, ANDROID_USE_LEGACY_TOOLCHAIN_FILE=false skips the legacy include-and-return branch; if the variable is undefined, the file defaults to legacy true and includes android-legacy.toolchain.cmake.

The legacy toolchain files set ANDROID_STL to c++_static only when it is not otherwise set and reject GNU STL/STLPort options; this is a conditional source-file rule, not proof of any final artifact's retained runtime code.
SHERPA_ONNX_LINK_LIBSTDCPP_STATICALLY is documented and guarded as a Linux static-build GNU libstdc++/libgcc option: it is evaluated only when BUILD_SHARED_LIBS is OFF and CMAKE_SYSTEM_NAME is Linux.

The supplied ELF observations are negative/limited: final SOs have DYNSYM and no SYMTAB, none has libc++_shared DT_NEEDED, and exported std::__ndk1 names show interface ABI namespace presence, not retained implementation, exact version, static absence, or complete composition.

prohibitedOverclaims: Final Sherpa or ORT binaries statically retain libc++/libc++abi/unwind code merely because an NDK legacy default or option default exists.
Final binaries use libc++_shared because CMAKE_CXX_FLAGS contains -stdlib=libc++, BUILD_SHARED_LIBS=ON, or no libc++_shared DT_NEEDED is observed.
SHERPA_ONNX_LINK_LIBSTDCPP_STATICALLY=OFF proves Android libc++ dynamic linkage; it is not the Android NDK STL selector.
ORT used the r27d legacy toolchain branch or legacy c++_static default despite explicitly passing ANDROID_USE_LEGACY_TOOLCHAIN_FILE=false.
Sherpa explicitly disabled the legacy toolchain, or explicitly set SHERPA_ONNX_LINK_LIBSTDCPP_STATICALLY=OFF for all four ABIs.
No SYMTAB, no libc++_shared DT_NEEDED, or absence of expected symbol names proves absence of hidden, inlined, stripped, or dlopened code.
Source-tag files alone prove the packaged NDK kit identity, final composition, or applicable full notices.
Reference-only local NDK 27.0.12077973 or 30.0.16138531-beta3 were the actual build toolchains.
These CMake/NDK excerpts close full notice applicability or legal acceptance.
